title: MerchantOps - Ops Lifecycle Health Check & Cost Acceleration
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost anomalies from a recent spike, latency regressions during peak checkout flows, and runway for next-model rollout. Agreed to run a short performance benchmark on dedicated pool and share quantization recommendation doc.
topics: usage trends and billing spike investigation
latency under 95th percentile during flash sales
dedicated vs hosted economics for checkout model
next-model rollout timeline and canary strategy
action_items: Noah Grant: Share internal billing spike dashboard and 24-hour logs - due 2025-11-03
Diego Ramos (Redwood SE): Run 2x dedicated pool benchmark focusing on 512->1024 token flows and send raw results - due 2025-11-06
Priya Malhotra (CSM): Send security pack (SOC2 excerpts + KMS integration notes) and onboarding checklist - due 2025-11-02
next_steps: Redwood to run dedicated benchmark and confirm latency/SLA delta vs hosted
MerchantOps to validate billing export and identify whether burst traffic correlated with third-party crawler
Schedule pilot for canary rollout of new 7B quantized model in staging next week
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Alright thanks everyone for hopping on, we wanna keep this tight—48 minutes on the calendar, quick health check for MerchantOps. Samir, do you wanna kick off with what you saw last week?
[00:16] Samir Patel: Yeah thanks Lena. Uh, we had a billing spike last Thursday, looked like about 3x normal token burn for two hours during the promo window. It coincided with higher tail latency on checkout recommendations. We flagged Redwood because the token delta seemed disproportionate to user traffic.
[00:35] Ava Lee: And to add, there was a small error surge—5xxs—mostly timeouts. Our SREs saw KV cache misses around the same window, so we're wondering if cache invalidation or model routing switched lanes.
[00:52] Diego Ramos: Hmm, interesting. We had a routing fallback for a short window in us-west-2 when a rack reported higher queue depths, that could explain a switch to a lower-capacity variant. I need to check the logs—I can pull the routing trace.
[01:10] Noah Grant: From the FinOps side, the invoice shows token metrics mapping to two different model SKUs; one is the hosted high-throughput SKU and one is the dedicated variant. Why did that happen? We thought the checkout calls were pinned to the dedicated pool.
[01:27] Lena Park: Good question. There are a couple of causes—either the pin on the route wasn't honored due to a transient metadata mismatch or Autoscale spilled requests onto hosted to keep latency SLOs. Diego, could autoscale have triggered a fallback?
[01:42] Diego Ramos: Yeah autoscale has a short fallback policy: if dedicated queue exceeds threshold, we can route to a hosted-compatible variant to avoid tail latency blowing up. That policy is configurable per route, but I recall MerchantOps left the default fallback enabled during onboarding.
[02:00] Samir Patel: Ah, that explains the SKU mix then. Can we get an audit of when that fallback executed?
[02:06] Diego Ramos: Yep I'll pull the routing trace and the policy evals — should show the exact timestamps.
[02:12] Ava Lee: Also want to understand the KV-cash—sorry KV cache—invalidate behaviour. On our side we clear some prefixes during deploy, could that cause thundering cache misses?
[02:25] Diego Ramos: Totally. If you purge shared prefixes right before a big promo, you can get a lot of cold starts. We do have prefix-level prewarming but it's best triggered from the deploy pipeline.
[02:37] Lena Park: Ok action: Noah to share billing extracts, Diego to pull routing traces, Priya will send the security pack.
[02:44] Priya Malhotra: I'll share the SOC2 summary and the KMS/HSM integration notes. Also, MerchantOps asked about SSO/JIT provisioning—I'll include the SAML SSO-runbook.
[02:58] Samir Patel: On the model side, we're preparing to roll a new 7B quantized model for checkout ranking. We expect improved throughput but need to verify latency under 95th pct. Any recommendations?
[03:14] Diego Ramos: For the 7B quant, we recommend a dedicated pool with 64-concurrency and disabled batching for checkout to keep p95 in check, or alternatively use continuous prefix caching. Quantized models can sometimes increase deterministic per-token latency due to memory packing if kernel selection isn't ideal.
[03:33] Ava Lee: Hmm, can you send the guidance as a checklist? We want specific config: batch size, concurrency, padding strategy.
[03:43] Diego Ramos: Yes—I'll send a benchmark plan. We'll run two profiles: checkout-style (short prompts, high QPS) and session-style (longer, chat flows).
[03:54] Noah Grant: Cost question—if we move checkout to dedicated, what's the delta in $/million tokens vs hosted? We want to justify a reserved-capacity commit.
[04:06] Lena Park: We can model this. Dedicated gives predictable per-token cost but has fixed capacity costs. For your usage pattern with high flash spikes, a small dedicated pool + burst to hosted can be cheaper than pure hosted. But because you saw spillover, we should look at dedicated sizing to avoid fallback.
[04:24] Samir Patel: Could we set an override to prevent fallback during a promo? Risk is higher latency if the dedicated pool saturates.
[04:33] Diego Ramos: You can, but it's risky—the system default prefers graceful degradation to keep endpoints up. Another option is a canary routing policy: keep a small pool pinned and a forced warm pool for promo windows.
[04:45] Ava Lee: That might work. We'll probably schedule a pre-warm job before promos.
[04:50] Lena Park: Great. Switching to security: MerchantOps asked about encryption at rest with customer-managed keys?
[04:58] Priya Malhotra: Yes, Redwood supports KMS integrations—both cloud KMS and customer-managed HSM workflows. There are a couple of caveats around snapshotting and key rotation windows. I'll surface the exact rotation SLA in the doc.
[05:12] Noah Grant: Do you support out-of-band audit logs for model payloads? We need to prove data residency for a subset of tenants.
[05:20] Priya Malhotra: We can emit audit events to your SIEM via syslog or direct S3 push with encryption, and you can request token-level logs for compliance. We'll include examples in the pack.
[05:31] Samir Patel: Back to the spike—Noah will share the billing slice but we also have a hypothesis: a third-party crawler hit an open API path and triggered lots of cold starts. Do you see increased volume from unknown IPs?
[05:45] Diego Ramos: I can look at request metadata but MerchantOps may want to block or rate-limit that path. We also support per-route WAF rules.
[05:54] Ava Lee: We'll check our edge and send logs.
[05:58] Lena Park: Ok, let's talk timeline for the model pilot. Samir, when do you want to start the canary?
[06:04] Samir Patel: Prefer next Tuesday — so basically one week from now. We want a small percent of traffic through the new model in staging, then a ramp in production if p95 and cost align.
[06:15] Diego Ramos: That timeline is doable. SE will run the dedicated benchmarks, and we'll prepare a rollout plan: feature-flagged canary, synthetic load test during off-peak, and automatic rollback on p95 breaches.
[06:29] Lena Park: Good. Any competitor pressure? Noah?
[06:33] Noah Grant: ZephyrAI pitched a lower per-request price but they don't have the same private deployment story. We're weighing a cost play vs security and operational guarantees.
[06:44] Priya Malhotra: I'll include a short comparison sheet—features vs cost and the Redwood differentiate points like dedicated pool SLAs and the routing fallback safety net.
[06:55] Ava Lee: On operational runbooks, we also need an oncall playbook for when KV cache spikes happen. Who owns that? Is it us or Redwood?
[07:04] Lena Park: It's a shared responsibility. We'll provide a runbook for diagnosing KV cache cold starts and triggering pre-warm; your SREs will run the pre-warm job. We'll put owners in the runbook.
[07:16] Samir Patel: Ok, can we also add a throttling plan for third-party bots? That should reduce token burn.
[07:22] Diego Ramos: We support per-route rate limits and token caps. We'll show config examples.
[07:29] Ava Lee: Great. Quick parking-lot: can we get a breakdown of the recent token consumption by model variant across the last 30 days?
[07:36] Lena Park: Yes, Redwood will export a usage CSV with model SKU columns. Priya will attach the security docs, Diego the benchmark plan, and Samir will provide the billing slice.
[07:48] Samir Patel: One more detail—the team noticed a small regression after the last runtime update; a 3% increase in 95th percentile. Is that likely from kernel selection changes?
[07:58] Diego Ramos: Possible. Kernel/compilation choices can affect p95; I'll look at the runtime telemetry. We keep previous kernel snapshots for rollbacks.
[08:10] Noah Grant: Okay timeline recap?
[08:12] Lena Park: Quick recap: Diego runs benchmarks by 11/06, Noah shares billing by 11/03, Priya sends security pack by 11/02. Pilot canary target next Tuesday. We'll meet again after the benchmark to finalize sizing—suggest 30 minutes.
[08:30] Ava Lee: Sounds good. Anything else?
[08:33] Samir Patel: No, thanks. Appreciate the quick triage.
[08:36] Priya Malhotra: I'll follow up with the doc links and a recommended config snippet for the 7B quant.
[08:43] Lena Park: Ok thanks everyone, we'll close.
[08:46] (call ends)
notes: Redwood to attach benchmark results and model quantization guidance
MerchantOps to validate edge logs for third-party crawler hypothesis
